newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas inches higher on colder weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas inches higher on colder weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices moved slightly higher Monday as colder weather in the East boosted heating demand, market sources said.
Temperatures in the Northeast are forecast to be about four to 12 degrees Fahrenheit below normal through Friday, Weather Services Corp reported.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices gained four cents to the high-$1.90s per mmBtu, with Henry Hub mostly at $2.00-2.02.
In south Texas, prices were similarly higher in the mid-$1.90s as temperatures in the state remained near- to as much as 11 degrees F above normal.
In the East, New York city-gate prices climbed about five cents into the mid-$2.30s to about $2.40 in anticipation of the extended cold in the region.
In the Appalachian region, prices rose by about two cents to $2.09-2.20.
In the Midcontinent, prices also firmed by about two cents to the low-$1.90s as colder temperatures were forecast for the northern part of the region by the middle of this week.
Demarcation was also quoted in the low-$1.90s, while Chicago city-gate values jumped to about $2.11-2.14, up more than 10 cents from Friday.

Detroit Edison said it had restored service to about 385,000 of its more than two million customers. The company estimated that about 422,000 customers were initially affected by last Thursday's ice storm-related outages.
Prices at the Detroit city-gate were talked mostly around $2.20.
Further west where temperatures have been hovering above normal, Permian basin prices were about three cents higher in the low-to-mid $1.80s. Waha was quoted mostly in the high-$1.80s.
The 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California was in "hot standby" this morning and expected to be back on line Monday night, Southern California Edison reported.
